title: Sven 9 Warriors

sources.label: HOW TO PLAY ★★★ Sven RAMPAGE Build In Auto Chess

body:
# Sven 9 Warriors

This is a nine-Warrior board that funnels all of its item and roll priority into
a single legendary carry: Sven. The engine is the Demon trait — as long as Sven
is the *only* Demon on the board, his normal attacks are settled as pure damage
that stacks Fel Power up to seven times, ignoring armor and magic resist
entirely. Layer that onto the 9-Warrior perk (which reflects pure damage equal
to 1.5× current armor and doubles Warrior armor below 50% HP) and Sven becomes a
tanky, armor-independent cleaving carry that racks up rampages. The build plays
as an early win-streak Warrior board that slowly upgrades every slot into a purple
or legendary Warrior, then techs in Gods and Nagas late for the mirror matchups.

## Core Units

| Unit | Cost | Synergies | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sven | 5 | Demon, Warrior | The carry — keep him the only Demon so his attacks deal pure damage |
| Axe | 1 | Orc, Warrior | Cheap early Warrior body |
| Mars | 1 | God, Warrior | Cheap Warrior that also enables the 2-God cooldown bonus |
| Juggernaut | 2 | Orc, Warrior | Early Warrior body and self-carry filler |
| Centaur Warrunner | 2 | Centaur, Warrior | Strong early Warrior tank |
| Tiny | 2 | Elemental, Warrior | Warrior body with a stun |
| Slardar | 3 | Naga, Warrior | Warrior that also opens the Naga magic-resist line |
| Huskar | 3 | Troll, Warrior | Warrior with built-in magic resist as he drops low |
| Kunkka | 4 | Human, Warrior | Purple Warrior body and AoE |
| Rubick | 3 | God, Wizard | Second God (with Mars) for team cooldown reduction |
| Medusa | 4 | Hunter, Naga | Second Naga (with Slardar) for magic resist plus a stone stun |

The core is nine distinct Warriors for the reflect/armor perk; Rubick adds the
2-God cooldown bonus alongside Mars, and Medusa pairs with Slardar for 2-Naga
magic resistance against mages.

## Items

Sven does not lack damage — his items are almost entirely defensive and utility,
because the whole plan is to keep him alive and mobile long enough to cleave the
backline. The priority stack is **Black King Bar** (mage immunity), **Linkens
Sphere** (blocks the single-target hexes and Doom that hard-counter a solo
carry), and **Blink Dagger** so he reaches the enemy casters instead of chasing
the front line all fight. Round out with **Guardian Greaves** (cleanses the mage
debuffs), **Monkey King Bar** for attack speed and to pierce evasion, and
**Aegis of Immortal** late for a second life. **Gossamer Cape** deserves a
special mention: its 25% magic resist also blocks the mind control from enemy
Priest boards, so keep one available if a 4-Priest player is in the lobby.

## Relics

**Leafy Essence** is the key pickup — it reduces roll costs, unlocks off-branch
synergies, and lets you push past level 10, all of which this deep-rolling build
leans on by round 35. **Doubloon** is a crucial late-game survival tool: it
converts your health/gold buffer into effective HP, which repeatedly saves the
game against the mage matchup when Sven can't win a fight outright. Economy
relics that protect the early win streak are also welcome.

## Leveling / Roll Plan

Open with a cheap Warrior win streak — two-star melee bodies plus the Warrior
armor bonus roll over most early boards, so sit at level 5 after round 6 for
interest and ride the streak for income. Ban Goblins (and later dilute the pool)
once you have 40+ surplus gold to raise your odds at purple Warriors and Sven.
The mid game is a long grind of upgrading Warrior slots to two-star and hunting
Sven copies. Three-starring Sven is the real win condition and it is *hard*:
there are only nine Sven in the pool and opponents contest him, so plan to fuse
extra copies with IO (a 5-cost Elf) or push to level 11 for the best legendary
odds. Don't three-star lesser Warriors — they aren't game-changing; bank rolls
for Sven and items instead.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Position Sven to reach the backline with Blink Dagger and cleave the important
casters (Zeus, Warlock, Keeper of the Light) before they cast; if he only ever
hits the front line, the enemy mages get too many casts off and you lose. Spread
your Warriors so a single AoE doesn't clip several at once, and keep Huskar at the
back where his low-HP magic resist makes him a soft anti-mage anchor. This is a
rock-paper-scissors comp in the ultra-late lobby: you beat mages thanks to BKB +
Naga magic resist, but you lose to a rival carry that also deals *pure* damage
(an enemy Sven, or a Cobalt duplication board with armor reduction), since your
own armor and reflect do nothing against pure damage. Hex and Doom on Sven are
the individual threats to answer — that's what Linkens Sphere and Guardian
Greaves are for.
